name: MaxText
description: A simple, performant, and scalable Jax LLM!
editorialSummary: Google's high-performance JAX LLM training reference (now under AI-Hypercomputer) for scalable pretraining on GPUs/TPUs. Practical JAX counterpart to PyTorch Megatron-style stacks.
whyCare: Best-known open JAX example stack for serious LLM training research and performance work.
notes: Formerly google/maxtext; GitHub canonical full_name is AI-Hypercomputer/maxtext.

name: RWKV-LM
description: RWKV (pronounced RwaKuv) is an RNN with great LLM performance, which can also be directly trained like a GPT transformer (parallelizable). We are at RWKV-7 "Goose". So it's combining the best of RNN and transformer - great performance, linear time, constant space (no kv-cache), fast training, infinite ctx_len, and free sentence embedding.
editorialSummary: Official research implementation of RWKV, the linear-time RNN/transformer hybrid architecture for LLMs. Demonstrates competitive language modeling without quadratic attention.
whyCare: Canonical code for studying and training alternative sequence architectures beyond softmax attention.

name: GPT-NeoX
description: An implementation of model parallel autoregressive transformers on GPUs, based on the Megatron and DeepSpeed libraries
editorialSummary: EleutherAI's large-scale GPT training codebase that powered open GPT-NeoX-20B and related open LM efforts. Combines Megatron-style parallelism with DeepSpeed.
whyCare: Key reference for open large-model training before today's many commercial stacks; still relevant for Megatron/DeepSpeed-style research setups.

name: Flax
description: Flax is a neural network library for JAX that is designed for flexibility.
editorialSummary: Google's flexible neural net library on JAX, widely used for research implementations that need composable transforms, clarity, and TPU/GPU portability. Home to many JAX/Flax example patterns for transformers and beyond.
whyCare: Go-to stack when a paper or lab ships JAX reference code and you need an idiomatic NN API rather than raw JAX.
notes: GitHub primary language reported as Jupyter Notebook; library code is Python/JAX.

name: The Annotated Transformer
description: An annotated implementation of the Transformer paper.
editorialSummary: Harvard NLP's line-by-line annotated reimplementation of Attention Is All You Need. The most cited pedagogical OSS companion to the original Transformer paper.
whyCare: Carefully preferred AIAYN learning artifact: pairs paper exposition with working code rather than a bare architecture clone.
notes: Chosen over many AIAYN clones for editorial quality and historical role in teaching transformers.

name: Transformers
description: 🤗 Transformers: the model-definition framework for state-of-the-art machine learning models in text, vision, audio, and multimodal models, for both inference and training.
editorialSummary: The de facto open-source model zoo and definition layer for modern transformers across NLP, vision, audio, and multimodal work. It turned research checkpoints into a shared, reproducible API used by labs and product teams alike.
whyCare: If you need to load, fine-tune, or publish SOTA pretrained models with a consistent interface, this is the research-to-production bridge most papers and tutorials assume.
notes: Seminal papers-with-code style hub; primaryCategory research despite broad training/inference use.

name: minGPT
description: A minimal PyTorch re-implementation of the OpenAI GPT (Generative Pretrained Transformer) training
editorialSummary: The precursor minimal GPT reimplementation that shaped how researchers teach and prototype transformer LMs. Intentionally tiny and readable rather than production-oriented.
whyCare: Still the clearest short codebase for studying GPT architecture and training before moving to nanoGPT or larger stacks.
notes: Largely superseded by nanoGPT for active experiments; retained for historical/educational significance.

name: nanoGPT
description: The simplest, fastest repository for training/finetuning medium-sized GPTs.
editorialSummary: Karpathy's minimal GPT training repo that became the default educational and prototyping baseline for modern LLM research. Small enough to read end-to-end, serious enough to train real models.
whyCare: Best starting point for understanding GPT training loops, scaling experiments, and reproducible medium-scale pretraining without framework overhead.

name: LitGPT
description: 20+ high-performance LLMs with recipes to pretrain, finetune and deploy at scale.
editorialSummary: Lightning AI's readable from-scratch LLM implementations with production-minded recipes for pretrain, finetune, and deploy. Emphasizes clarity over framework magic while staying competitive on throughput.
whyCare: Useful when you want research-grade LLM training code that is still approachable enough to hack on without Megatron-scale complexity.

name: x-transformers
description: A concise but complete full-attention transformer with a set of promising experimental features from various papers
editorialSummary: Phil Wang (lucidrains) library packing many experimental attention/transformer paper ideas into a compact, hackable PyTorch implementation. A frequent research playground for trying architectural variants quickly.
whyCare: Ideal when you want paper features (attention variants, positional schemes, etc.) composed without rebuilding a transformer from scratch.

name: Mamba
editorialSummary: Official implementation of Mamba selective state-space models, a major post-Transformer architecture paper with strong long-sequence efficiency claims. Reference CUDA/PyTorch research code from the authors.
whyCare: The source of truth for reproducing Mamba and building SSM-based language/sequence models.

name: S4
editorialSummary: Official Structured State Space (S4) sequence model repository—the influential SSM research line that preceded Mamba. Core papers-with-code artifact for long-range sequence modeling without full attention.
whyCare: Read this to understand the SSM lineage and baselines before Mamba and later selective SSMs.

name: Tensor2Tensor
description: Library of deep learning models and datasets designed to make deep learning more accessible and accelerate ML research.
editorialSummary: Google's historical TensorFlow research library that popularized reproducible Transformer and seq2seq experiments after Attention Is All You Need. Archived, but foundational to the papers-with-code era.
whyCare: Important lineage artifact for Transformer research tooling; superseded by Trax/Flax/JAX and modern libraries but historically significant.
notes: Archived; retained as historically significant Transformer-era research implementation library.
